history.cultural: In DoroszlÃ³, KlÃ¡ber is played at custom-made tables with built-in slate for scoring (using chalk, not paper). The game is considered part of the cultural heritage of ethnic Hungarians in the region. Players traditionally cut the deck to settle random decisions, including who goes out for more wine.
history.evolution: The game evolved from Klabberjass but adapted to the Hungarian card deck. The unique meld system (sequences, sets, and bella) and the anti-clockwise play direction reflect Hungarian card game traditions.

setup.players: 4 players in fixed partnerships, teammates sitting opposite each other.
setup.deck: 32-card Hungarian deck (William Tell/Seasons pattern) with German suits: Acorns (Makk), Leaves (ZÃ¶ld), Hearts (Piros), and Gourds (TÃ¶k). Cards: Ace, King, Over Knave, Under Knave, Ten, Nine, Eight, Seven.
setup.dealing: Deal anti-clockwise in batches (not more than 3 cards at a time). Each player receives 8 cards: first 5 cards dealt, then a separate 3 cards. The last three must be kept separate from the first five until after bidding.

rules.objective: Score points by winning tricks containing valuable cards and by declaring meld combinations. The team that chooses trumps must take more than half the total card points (81+ out of 161) plus any meld points.
rules.gameplay: Play is anti-clockwise. Must follow suit if possible. If cannot follow, may play any card. Highest trump wins; if no trump, highest card of led suit wins. The last trick is worth 10 extra points.
keyRules: Player to dealer's right must bid 1 first; bidding proceeds counterclockwise.
Follow suit if possible; if void in led suit must play trump if able; otherwise any card.
Trick won by highest trump, or highest card of led suit if no trump. Winner leads next trick.
Last trick worth 10 extra card points. Contractor's team must take more than half of 161 card points plus melds.
First team to 501 points wins the game. Maccs (double game) if winners have 501+ and opponents under 251.

strategy.basic: In the bidding, remember that the player to dealer's right is forced to bid '1'. If you have strength in Acorns, you may be able to compete for the contract. Hold the Over (Jack) and Nine of trumps if possibleâ€”they are worth 34 points together.
strategy.intermediate: Meld declaration is crucial. Sequences (Terc, Kvart, etc.) and sets (Four Aces, Four Overs) can add significant points. The Bella (King and Over of trumps) is worth 40 points and nearly always scores. Plan your play to win tricks where you can claim meld points.
strategy.advanced: The Kontra round (if played) allows opponents to double the stakes if they believe the bidding team will fail. Understand when to Kontra based on your hand strength. Manage your trump cards carefullyâ€”the Over and Nine are powerful but using them at the right time is key.

scoring.description: Each hand: team with more card points (tricks plus last-trick bonus) and meld points wins. Game (parti): first team to reach 501 or more wins. If both pass 501 in same hand, contractor's team wins. Maccs (double game) if winners have 501+ and opponents under 251.
scoring.winCondition: Team that takes more than half of 161 card points plus meld wins the hand; first team to 501 points wins the game.
